scoreScale.plain: how decisively the firing ends up on the correct side of the body

rungPlain.withdraw: A brief poke on one side of the body; the activity has to end up on the opposite side. The far side cannot feel the poke, so word of it has to travel across the body.
rungPlain.context: Face the light, unless a small local cue is present on that trial, in which case face away. Most cells cannot feel the cue, so they have to be told.
rungPlain.jump: Two flashes, A then B, at different spots; point the way the flash jumped. How the body answers B has to depend on where A was, so the A-site has to tell the B-site.
rungPlain.memory: A flash, then a dark wait of random length, then a uniform 'go' signal; point where the flash was. The memory has to outlast what one cell can hold by itself.

founderPicking.old: old founder picking: the run started from the fittest of 1,024 random genomes, so it could start from a dead single cell that never fires (fitness is score minus energy cost, and silence costs almost nothing)
founderPicking.partly fixed: partly fixed: sampling went on until some genome scored at least 0.05, but founders were still chosen by fitness, so a dead single cell could still win
founderPicking.fixed: fixed (after the code review): genomes that actually score are chosen first, so no dead starts
founderPicking.not applicable: random search: no founders, it just keeps the best of all the genomes it tried

needs_messages.title: Do the solutions really depend on cells talking to their neighbours?
needs_messages.plain: For each task, the best evolved body is tested twice on the same 48 unseen test trials: once normally, and once with its cells deaf to their neighbours. A third bar is a separate evolution run where the cells could never hear each other at all. That third bar mostly shows evolution giving up: 6 of its 9 runs ended as one cell that never fires, and on context and jump known message-free tricks do a little better (0.17 and about 0.13), so the strong evidence is the second bar.
needs_messages.measure: held-out score (48 unseen trials; 1 = all firing on the correct side, 0 = no lean or silence)

evolvedWithMessagesOff.note: Evolved from 1 founder (the setup of the original baseline sweeps), not 8, with the old founder picking. 2 of 3 seeds ended as a single cell that never fires, and in 3 of 3 no starting genome even beat its energy cost. So this bar shows that evolution without messages found nothing here, not that 0 is the best possible without messages: the best known message-free trick scores 0.02, about what these runs reached (README 'Message rungs' table; the README does not say which trials).

baselines.title: Is evolution better than the simple alternatives?
baselines.plain: Every condition got the same number of tries (about 52,000 bodies tested). Random search just tries 52,000 random genomes and keeps the best. The fixed disk skips growth: the body is a ready-made round patch of identical cells, and only the cell's firing rule evolves.
baselines.measure: held-out score (48 unseen trials) in values/median; 'valid' is the same body on 48 fresh trials like the training ones; 'cells' is body size; 'types' is how many of the 4 cell types the body uses

baselines.note: Each cell's 'founderPicking' says which version of the starting-genome code the run used (see the top-level 'founderPicking' legend). The 8-founder bars mix all three: withdraw_v2 'fixed', context_lattice 'partly fixed', jump_f8 'old'. All 1-founder, fixed-disk and messages-off runs use 'old'. On withdraw this matters: with the old code seed 2 started from a dead single cell and scored 0.00 (withdraw_evo).

breeding.title: Does mixing two parents (crossover) beat copying one parent with small changes (mutation only)?
breeding.plain: Crossover builds a child from whole pieces of two parents' genomes, like breeding. Mutation only copies one parent and tweaks a couple of numbers. Each pair is the same setup with only that switch flipped, three seeds each. Seed s of a pair starts from exactly the same founders in both modes; only the breeding switch differs after that, so each seed pair is a matched twin. That is also why a dead start (withdraw seed 2) is dead in both modes.

pairs.note: These withdraw runs (withdraw_f8, crossover median 0.381) are not the withdraw bar in the other charts (withdraw_v2, median 0.517), although both are 'hex, 8 founders, crossover'. The only difference is founder picking: withdraw_f8 used the old code, so seed 2 started from a dead single cell and scores 0.0 in both modes here; withdraw_v2 used the fixed code and has no dead start. withdraw_v2 has no mutation-only twin, so this comparison has to use withdraw_f8.

breeding.note: The jump_f8asex and withdraw_f8asex folders are named hex_sex_s* but their config.yaml says breeding: asex (the switch was a command-line override).

ladder.title: Climbing the ladder: withdraw, then context, then jump, then memory
ladder.plain: One population trains on a task until its best body scores 0.7 on fresh trials, then moves to the next task. In the second version, when it moves up, half the population is replaced by newcomers: random genomes picked because they already do a little on the new task.
ladder.checkpointNote: A checkpoint every 10 generations plus the last one (799). 'valid' and 'heldout' are scored on the rung the run was on at that checkpoint (48 trials each). At an advance generation the row still shows the old rung, because the score that triggered the advance was measured there. No per-checkpoint median is given: different seeds sit on different rungs at the same generation, so a median would mix tasks.
ladder.finalNote: finalValid and finalHeldout (from results.jsonl) are measured again at the end of the run on a new draw of 48 trials (src/run.py, random seed + 20000), so they do not equal the last checkpoint at generation 799 (from curves.jsonl, which draws its trials from seed + 5000 and seed + 10000). Same body, different trials: e.g. ladder_msg seed 2 valid 0.153 at the last checkpoint vs 0.110 final. Each seed's 'lastCheckpoint' is given next to its finals; if a curve is drawn to 799, show the final number as a separate marker, not as the curve's end point.
ladder.outcome: 5 of 6 runs pass withdraw and then stay on context for the rest of the run, never reaching jump or memory; the sixth (ladder_msg_imm seed 1) passes context and then stalls on jump.

runs.label: with newcomers on each new rung

lastRungSummary.plain: On jump (reached at generation 50), validation stays near 0 until generation 380, then sits between 0.10 and 0.38 (median 0.25). Held-out never goes above 0.15 (peak at generation 480) and ends at -0.02: what it learned on the training trials does not carry over to unseen ones.

census.title: What do completely random genomes already manage?
census.plain: 2,048 random genomes per grid shape, each grown and tested on 48 unseen trials of each original task; the table keeps the best one per task. It shows where the easy tasks end: random genomes already nearly solve 'face the light', but not the later ones.

taskPlain.light: face a light that comes from a random direction
taskPlain.brightness: the same, with the light anywhere from 10 times dimmer to 10 times brighter than normal (these are held-out trials; training uses 5 times dimmer to 5 times brighter)
taskPlain.memory: point where a flash was, after a dark wait
taskPlain.motion: point the way a moving spot travels
taskPlain.flicker: point at the faster-flickering of two lights

census.perSeed: not applicable: one census run (config seed 0) per lattice

reference.label: hand-built 'fire where lit' disk, no messages (RESULTS.md, enforced in tests/test_tasks.py)

references.source: README.md 'Message rungs' table and RESULTS.md 'message rungs built and red-teamed'
references.note: Single hand-built organisms (no seeds). The README does not say which trial split these were scored on.

notes: Scores: 1 means all firing sits on the correct side, 0 means no lean (or silence), negative means the wrong side. 'Held-out' = 48 trials the body never trained on (new directions, wider ranges). 'Valid' = 48 fresh trials like the training ones. Final numbers come from outputs/<sweep>/<run>/results.jsonl; where an aggregate exists (results/<rung>/results.csv) every number was cross-checked against it and matched.
Three seeds per condition, so medians of 3 values: differences under about 0.1-0.15 are within seed noise.

Runs that predate the code review fixes (RESULTS.md, 'code review'): memory_sweep, memory_random, memory_fixed, all withdraw/context/jump _evo/_random/_fixed/_nomsg, all _f8/_f8asex/_f8m4/_f8t24 runs, and context_lattice. Only withdraw_v2, ladder_msg and ladder_msg_imm use the fixed code.

The fix that matters most for these charts is founder picking (how the starting genomes are chosen). There are three versions, and every result cell carries a 'founderPicking' field naming its version (legend at the top level): 'old' (all 1-founder sweeps, the fixed disks, messages-off runs, jump_f8*, withdraw_f8*), 'partly fixed' (context_lattice: launched just before the fix landed, so its logs lack the 'scoring_founders' field and founders were still chosen by fitness), and 'fixed' (withdraw_v2, ladder_msg, ladder_msg_imm). With the old code withdraw seed 2 started from a dead single cell, which is why it scores 0.00 in withdraw_evo and in every withdraw_f8* variant. The other review findings (ladder trial mixing, flicker balance, plotting) do not touch the numbers used here.

The same label, 'withdraw, hex, 8 founders, crossover', appears with two numbers: median 0.381 in the breeding chart (withdraw_f8, old founder picking, seed 2 dead) and 0.517 in the messages and baselines charts (withdraw_v2, fixed founder picking). Same setup otherwise; only withdraw_f8 has a mutation-only twin, so the breeding chart must use it. The page should name the run (or the founder picking) wherever withdraw appears.

The 1-founder sweeps (*_evo, *_random, *_fixed, *_nomsg, memory_*) predate the switch to 8 founders. The 'evolved with messages off' bars therefore use 1 founder, while the 'messages on' bars use 8 founders (except memory). Messages-off evolution ends near 0 on all three message rungs (max 0.025).

The 'evolved with messages off' bars show that evolution without messages found nothing, not that 0 is the best possible without messages. In 6 of the 9 runs the final body is a single cell that never fires (cells: withdraw [6, 1, 1], context [1, 1, 7], jump [1, 1, 4]). In all 3 withdraw runs and in context seed 0, no starting genome even beat its energy cost (the old founder-picking problem). The best known message-free tricks score 0.17 on context and about 0.13 on jump (README 'Message rungs' table), more than these runs reached. The conclusion still holds; the strong evidence is the same evolved bodies dropping to 0.00 when their messages are switched off.

Memory has no messages-off evolution sweep and no 8-founder run. Also, memory's *training* delays can be partly solved by one slow cell type without messages (valid about 0.5, RESULTS.md review table), so a messages-off memory sweep would not necessarily end at 0 on fresh training-like trials; all evolved memory bodies do score 0.00 without messages on held-out trials.
Memory is easy: random search and the fixed one-type disk do as well as evolution there, so it shows that messages are needed but not that growth is.

Breeding pairs are matched twins: seed s starts from exactly the same founders with crossover and with mutation only (identical 'founders' lines in logs/, on all 24 seed pairs), and only the breeding switch differs after that. The *_f8asex folders are named hex_sex_s*, but their config.yaml says breeding: asex (command-line override). memory_sweep's crossover vs mutation-only comparison uses 1 founder; the context, jump and withdraw pairs use 8.

context_lattice square4 seed 0 ends near 0 in both breeding modes (founders scored only about 0.11), which drags those two medians' minimums down; memory_sweep square8 seed 2 (crossover) has valid 0.84 but held-out 0.00 (it did not generalize).

Ladder: 'valid' is on the current rung only (48 trials), while training fitness mixes 12 new-rung trials with 4 revisited earlier-rung trials. ladder_msg had no newcomers (its config has no immigrants key; the repo's configs/ladder_msg.yaml was later edited to add immigrants: 0.5 for ladder_msg_imm). 5 of 6 runs pass withdraw and then stay on context for the rest of the run, never reaching jump or memory; the sixth (ladder_msg_imm seed 1) passes context and then stalls on jump. ladder_msg_imm seed 1: On jump (reached at generation 50), validation stays near 0 until generation 380, then sits between 0.10 and 0.38 (median 0.25). Held-out never goes above 0.15 (peak at generation 480) and ends at -0.02: what it learned on the training trials does not carry over to unseen ones.

Ladder final scores (finalValid, finalHeldout) are re-measured at the end on a new draw of 48 trials, so they differ a little from the generation-799 checkpoint (e.g. ladder_msg seed 2 valid 0.153 vs 0.110). Show them as separate markers, not as the end of the curve.

Census numbers are transcribed from RESULTS.md (no stored output file). Each is the maximum over 2,048 genomes on the same 48 held-out trials it is reported on, so it is an optimistic (best-of-many) number. The census predates the flicker direction-balance fix, so its flicker column may be slightly inflated.
Tiny values like 1e-9 in heldout_no_messages are floating-point noise and are rounded to 0.
